# Vision Zero DC — Full Context

> Public-interest tool that turns official Washington, DC open crash data into a readable safety picture and evidence-backed policy recommendations. Static site (HTML/CSS/JS + a Python pipeline), no backend. This file gives an LLM enough context to use the data and pages correctly without fetching everything.

Current live numbers are NOT hardcoded here — read them from data/crash-summary.json so this file never goes stale.

## What the project answers

1. Where are people injured or killed on DC streets?
2. Which corridors, intersections, and modes face the highest risk?
3. What interventions are best supported by the evidence?
4. What changed after a policy, camera, redesign, or project?

Editorial promise (see CLAUDE.md): every numeric claim links to a primary source; separate observed facts from estimates and judgments; recommendations are transparent evidence cards, never opaque scores; avoid victim-blaming language; surface missingness; report wins alongside failures.

## Pages

- index.html — Safety Overview (logic: landing.js). Renders, from crash-summary.json: an accountability scorecard (A2), a deaths-vs-injuries trend (A3), KSI by travel mode (A4), and a "where harm concentrates" headline (A1); plus recommendation cards (from recommendations.json) and a countermeasure library (from countermeasures.json).
- map.html — Crash Map (logic: app.js). Live Leaflet map querying DC ArcGIS directly, with date/severity/mode/KSI filters, hot spots, ward crash-rate table, moving-violations overlay, and per-crash case files. Filters + map view serialize to the URL query string (date, sev, mode, viol, vmonth, ksi, c=lat,lng, z=zoom).
- hotspots.html — High-Injury Corridors (logic: hotspots.js). Leaflet map + profile cards for the highest-injury corridors from data/hotspots.geojson (severity, mode breakdown, recommended interventions, equity notes, confidence). Per-corridor counts are real — pipeline/hotspots.py joins crash records to the DDOT High Injury Network (crashes within 25 m of the centerline, 2022-present); full per-corridor data for all 77 HIN corridors is in data/hin-corridors.json.
- anc.html — ANC Safety Brief (logic: anc.js). Community-led prioritization: a ward selector drives a per-ward crash snapshot (from crash-summary.json), ALL High Injury Network corridors that run through the ward ranked by that ward's KSI (from data/hin-corridors.json, shown top-5 with a "show all" disclosure), and ward-scoped + citywide recommendations (from recommendations.json), then generates an editable, source-grounded resolution draft with copy / open-in-email (mailto, un-sent) / print actions. Static, no backend. Deep-linkable via #ward-N.
- src/crash-logic.js — shared pure logic (severity math, triage score, URL encode/decode), unit-tested in Node.

## Data dictionary — data/crash-summary.json

Top level: `schema_version`, `captured_at` (ISO), `generator`, `sources` (with query/page URLs), `method` (triage formula + notes), `caveats` (array), `scorecard`, `citywide_by_year` (array), `windows` (object keyed by date range).

- `windows[key]` for key in {"2024","2025","2026","all"}: `label`, `since`, `citywide` (crashes, fatalities, major_injuries, minor_injuries, pedestrians_involved, bicycles_involved, speeding_involved), `ksi_by_mode` (array of {mode, vulnerable, fatalities, major_injuries, ksi}), and `wards` (array, sorted by triage_score) where each ward has: ward, crashes, fatalities, major_injuries, minor_injuries, pedestrians_involved, bicycles_involved, speeding_involved, triage_score, population, land_area_sq_mi, crashes_per_100k, crashes_per_sq_mi, ksi_per_100k, ksi_per_sq_mi. The "Unknown ward" bucket merges records with missing/unparseable ward labels (meaningful missingness — do not drop).
- `scorecard`: baseline_window [2015,2019] and recent_window [2020,2024] averages for fatalities and ksi; latest_full_year + its fatalities/ksi; peak_recent_year/fatalities; preliminary_years; ytd_*; target_year (2024); data_quality note.
- `citywide_by_year`: {year, crashes, fatalities, major_injuries, minor_injuries, ksi} for 2015–present.

## Methodology

- Triage score (screening heuristic, NOT an official DDOT ranking; components always visible): crashes + 40*fatalities + 12*major_injuries + 2*minor_injuries + 2*pedestrians_involved + 2*bicycles_involved + 1*speeding_involved.
- KSI = fatalities + major (serious) injuries.
- Exposure rates use ward population (per 100k) and ward land area computed from official 2022 ward polygons via a local equirectangular projection (per sq mi). Per-area is preferred over per-capita because DC wards are drawn toward equal population.
- Scorecard accountability framing uses the settled 2020–2024 window (the 2015 open-data major-injury counts look anomalously high) and flags the most recent two years as preliminary because counts rise as records are coded.

## Key caveats (do not present as settled without checking)

- Open police-reported crash counts may differ from DDOT's curated Vision Zero figures.
- The most recent ~2 years are preliminary (reporting lag).
- Ward population values are ~2022 ward-level estimates on the 2022 ward boundaries (consistent with crash ward assignment), compiled from DC Office of Planning / DC Health Matters figures via a secondary compilation and anchored to the 2020 U.S. Census total of 689,545 (redistricting balanced each ward toward ~86,193, +/-5%); reconfirm each value against the DC OP per-ward tables before final public analysis.
- Countermeasure effect sizes are transcribed from cited sources and flagged unverified until re-checked.
- The "where harm concentrates" headline on the Overview page is ward-grain; the stronger street-segment "X% of streets = Y% of KSI" figure still needs the citywide crashes↔HIN share. The per-corridor hotspot counts (hotspots.html, hin-corridors.json) ARE now from a crashes↔High Injury Network spatial join (pipeline/hotspots.py).
- Moving-violation records are enforcement tickets, not crashes.

## Regenerating the data

`python3 pipeline/snapshot.py` (add `--refresh` to bypass the on-disk cache) fetches per-ward and per-year statistics from the DC ArcGIS endpoints, computes ward area + rates, joins denominators, and writes data/crash-summary.json with a pre-write sanity gate. Tests: `python3 tests/test_snapshot.py` and `node --test`.

## Authoritative sources

- Open Data DC — Crashes in DC: https://opendata.dc.gov/datasets/DCGIS::crashes-in-dc (ArcGIS layer .../Public_Safety_WebMercator/MapServer/24)
- Open Data DC — Crash Details Table: .../Public_Safety_WebMercator/MapServer/25
- DDOT Vision Zero: https://visionzero.dc.gov/
- DDOT Vision Zero crash analysis: https://visionzero.dc.gov/pages/crash-analysis
- DC Vision Zero crash dashboard: https://dcvisionzero.github.io/Crash-Injury-Dashboard/
- Ward 2022 boundaries (DCGIS): .../Administrative_Other_Boundaries_WebMercator/MapServer/53
